chunks: Among what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abi Ibrahim عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the junub and the menstruating woman touching with their hands the white dirhams. He said: “There is no harm.”

Because it is not impossible that he only permitted that for him when the name of Allah, Exalted is He, was not upon them, even if they were white dirhams; whereas the earlier report forbade it when there was something of that upon them. Then he said, may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: and he should not touch the Qur'an.
What indicates that is His saying, Exalted is He: “None touch it except the purified.”

So He prohibited touching the Book when taharah is absent. If someone were to say: this commits you to not permitting one who does not have minor ritual purity to touch the Qur'an, it would be said to him: that is indeed what we say; rather, we only permit him to touch the margins of the mushaf, but as for the written text itself, we do not permit it, and that is indicated by this.

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ: the divine name of Allah written on an object
key_terms.الطَّهَارَةِ الصُّغْرَى: minor ritual purity, typically attained through wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an, especially its written text in this context
key_terms.الْمُطَهَّرُونَ: those purified, cited in the Qur'anic proof-text
key_terms.حَوَاشِيَ الْمُصْحَفِ: the margins or outer areas of the written codex

ai.seo_question: Can a person without ritual purity touch coins bearing Allah’s name or the written text of the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on a junub or a menstruating woman touching silver coins and distinguishes between coins that bear the name of Allah and those that do not. It further establishes that touching the written text of the Qur'an is not permitted without taharah, citing the verse “None touch it except the purified,” while allowing contact with the margins of the mushaf.
